name: Yaesu FT-270R
notes: 2 m submersible handheld (~2007). Not to be confused with the unrelated 1980s FT-270R/FT-270RH 25 W mobile; if a spec sheet says 25 W or 13.8 VDC it is the mobile. Figures come from the Chicago-Offline ft270-277-info repo (SPECS.md, PROGRAMMING-TOOLS.md) and from CHIRP's VX-170 driver, which is the transport: the FT-270R is the amateur-branded sibling of the Vertex VX-170 and shares the FT-7800-family clone format (chirp/drivers/vx170.py inherits ft7800.FTx800Radio). max_channels 200 is the driver's memory_bounds (1, 200) and its memory[200] struct, and matches the published 200-memory figure. max_channel_name_chars 6 is the driver's names[200] struct with char name[6] — these are six-character alphanumeric tags, far shorter than any of our Chinese radios, so display names need aggressive shortening. modes is ["FM"]: the driver declares MODES ["FM", "NFM"] and has no AM. bandwidths_khz 12.5/25 follows that FM/NFM split. The TX band is the US amateur 2 m allocation 144-148 MHz; the wider 137-174 MHz span is the driver's valid_bands and is marked rx_only because stock firmware will not transmit outside the ham band and no MARS/CAP procedure has been verified for this model. max_zones is 1 as a profile-0.1 compatibility shim: the VX-170 driver sets has_bank = False, so memory banks are not reachable through the CHIRP path even though the chassis has them. NOT HARDWARE VERIFIED: the driver hard-checks the clone image model ID ('AH022$'), so a stock CHIRP may reject an FT-270R image; the pending CHIRP patch adds the real model string. Verify against a physical radio before trusting a write.
